Thanks Andrew — we can do 11:30 PT. I've attached our operational checklist and the keystore handoff instructions; short summary below.

High-level plan (30m bridge):
1) Keystore handshake (5-8m) — exchange test token; validate decrypt on a canary host.
2) Network fingerprint confirmation (5m) — we run a connectivity probe to your ingress/NAT and confirm return path and AS path.
3) KV cache priming (10m) — we run a scripted prefix warmup then sample cache hit metrics.
4) Quick smoke (5m) — generate sample traffic and validate latency/throughput targets and fallbacks.

Attachments: redwood-runbook-v2.pdf, keystore-transfer-instructions.txt

Pre-reqs from Aurora:
- A short-lived KMS test token (or service principal) for the handshake.
- Designated ops contact on the bridge (ops-eng@aurora-sys.com is perfect).

I'll be on the bridge with Laura and Aditya — sending calendar invite now.

Date: 2026-11-23T15:30:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Aurora bridge playbook + quick assertions (INF-4781)

Team — recap from the morning bridge scheduling. This is internal prep for the 11:30PT bridge tomorrow.

Playbook highlights (compact):
- Step A: Validate keystore decryption on the canary (host: canary01). Success criteria: app decrypts sample secret and returns 200 in <500ms.
- Step B: Run traffic fingerprint probe (script: net-fingerprint.sh) against Aurora ingress IPs. Look for symmetric path and no unexpected RSTs.
- Step C: KV priming: run prefix_warmup.py for 10 minutes; target 90% hit ratio on sampled keys.
- Step D: Smoke: 50 concurrent requests session, measure p50/p95 latency; fallback to model-variant (cpu) should not exceed 2x latency.

Incident/rollback triggers:
- Keystore handshake fails twice -> abort and fall back to preserved key material, loop in Security.
- Network probes show asymmetric return path or >1% packet loss -> pause and escalate to Network.
- KV hit ratio <50% after priming -> extend warmup and delay traffic cutover.

Attachments: smoke-test-assertions.md
JIRA: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4781

Please confirm who will own each step; I'm volunteering to run the KV priming and the smoke harness.

Chloe
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Lane <andrew.lane@aurora-sys.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T11:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: final validation checklist & keystore handoff — post-launch readout

Hi Andrew (and team),

Good news — flip completed at 11:05 PT. Quick readout:

- Keystore handshake: completed successfully. Test decrypt on canary01 returned 200; no errors in KMS audit.
- Network fingerprint: probes returned symmetric paths, no unexpected RSTs; egress NAT observed as planned.
- KV priming: 12-minute run; sampled hit ratio stabilized at 93%.
- Smoke tests: 50 concurrent sessions, p50=82ms, p95=310ms, error rate 0.2% (within SLA). No automatic fallback triggered.

Attached: kv_warmup.log (sample), smoke-test-assertions.md (results).

Next steps:
- We'll monitor token-level cost and latency dashboards for the first 12 hours and do another sampling at +6h and +12h.
- If anything above threshold appears, we'll run targeted rollbacks per INF-4781.

Thanks for the smooth ops handoff — Andrew, please let us know if Aurora wants a 30-min postmortem later this week.

Laura Bennett
Principal Ops Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
